values: The Part I effluent limits table for Total Dissolved Solids, Net Increase, listing both 497 mg/L and 449 mg/L with footnotes *10 and *11 defining phased applicability periods relative to the permit effective date.

grounding.selected_observations[1].excerpt: Total Dissolved Solids, Net Increase table rows showing 497 mg/L (*10) and 449 mg/L (*11)
Footnote *10: limits begin on the effective date of this permit and lasting through 3 years from the permit effective date
Footnote *11: limits apply during the period beginning 3 year from the permit effective date and lasting through the expiration date of the permit

rationale: The packet excerpt from Part I pages 5–6 directly shows two Total Dissolved Solids, Net Increase effluent-limit rows (497 mg/L with footnote *10 and 449 mg/L with footnote *11) and footnotes *10 and *11 that phase those numeric limits relative to the permit effective date. The proposition in values is therefore established by the evidence. Note: the packet does not include the permit effective date or Federal FY2025 monitoring measurements, so the broader why_demanded question—whether the compliance-schedule language alone establishes which limit applies for each FY2025 monitoring period—remains outside what this disposition resolves; only the table-and-footnote structure described in values is adjudicated here.
